message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of these reliable sources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Live AQI readings, pollutant breakdowns, health advisories | Go to [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/), enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Global map, historical trends, forecast | Visit [aqicn.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/), and you’ll see the current AQI and pollutant levels. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, CBS Los Angeles) | Often embed live AQI widgets | Search “Los Angeles air quality” on their websites. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., AirVisual, Plume Labs) | Push notifications, personalized alerts | Download the app, set Los Angeles as your location, and enable notifications. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, the AirNow website usually updates every 15–30 minutes, so it’s a good place to start.
message.reasoning: User asks about current air quality in Los Angeles. We need to provide real-time data. We don't have real-time data. We can suggest checking AirNow or local sources. We can provide general info. No tool needed.
